There had to have been a better way to grow crops before Monsanto/GMO.
What are some good alternatives to pesticides on crops?

What crops are you wanting to grow?

Pesticides can also be OMRI listed (that is that they are certified for organic use).

I grow a lot of crops (all Non-GMO) and I only use OMRI sprays. I get a lot of my sprays from here.

You can look at some cultural methods of removing pests. The best bet would be to include a variety of methods, which would include using chemicals.

 -Crop Rotation (throws off disease, insect and some weed cycles)

 -Pesticides (herbicides, fungicides, and insecticides. Extremely effective)

 -Mechanical (tillage. Can help kill weeds)

 -Cultural (mainly preventative measures. Delayed seeding, higher seeding rate, smaller seed spacing to make your crop more competitive, etc.)

 -Biological (you can get some insects that will only target specific weeds. Example: A type of flea beetle in Leafy Spurge)

If you have a good mixture of all these methods, you will do fine as a farmer without being over reliant on pesticides. But you would be a fool not to use pesticides when required to.
Ladybugs and mantises can be orderws online in bulk.

We use several methods.

First we tilled annually most areas but have scaled back to every other year now.

We also burn areas to prevent over wintered pests every other year. These two methods also destroy beneficial bacteria and beneficial insects so we have been doing them less.

We have deep mulching on most of our plants.

We rotate all crops on a four year cycle.

We plant crops closer together than average and plant them a lot earlier than most other people in our area. We have lost some things to frost, but it has been minimal.

We also generally plant 20-30 percent more than we expect to need. This hasn't always worked out as we keep underestimating how much we will need.

We do hand pick pests off of some crops, in particular tomatoes. This isn't always possible though. We hand weed most of our land....with help. Mulching is a necessity or this would not be remotely possible.

For other plants we use Diatomaceous Earth dusted onto the leaves about twice a month. This does not work for all pests though, so we also have to lay down Bt, and wash about twice a month with soap water on the leaves. It's pretty easy if we just spray it. Sometimes we also have to spray with hot pepper oil because local critters have found our harvest so tempting.
